design_signals.statement: Browser code retains reusable authentication credentials in script-readable storage. Script execution in the same origin can obtain the credentials and reuse the authenticated session.
design_signals.title: Browser scripts retain reusable session credentials

design_signals.statement: Document-store queries take operators or JavaScript predicates from application values instead of fixed query structures with typed values. Callers can change what a query selects, for example through injected operators or evaluated expressions.
design_signals.title: Document-database queries take their structure from application values

design_signals.statement: Document-store queries take operators or JavaScript predicates from application values instead of fixed query structures with typed values. Callers can change what a query selects, for example through injected operators or evaluated expressions.
design_signals.title: Document-database queries take their structure from application values

design_signals.statement: An interpreter evaluates application values as code. The affected path mixes data processing with executable program construction instead of constraining callers to predefined operations.
design_signals.title: Application data crosses into executable code

design_signals.statement: The client starts OAuth or OpenID Connect sign-in without a per-request state value that its callback verifies. A forged authorization response can then complete sign-in in the victim's browser with the attacker's grant.
design_signals.title: OAuth sign-in requests are not bound to the user's browser session

design_signals.statement: A state-changing operation accepts ambient browser credentials without an enforced check that the authenticated user initiated the request. The affected mutation path lacks a request-authenticity boundary.
design_signals.title: Cookie-authenticated changes lack request authenticity checks
